page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-2 is an entry-level, compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the E2 instance family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core and 2 threads on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with a dedicated CPU allocation, 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It includes 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the e2-highcpu-2 in the lower tiers of performance. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved a single-core CPU score of 1105.98 (bottom 25%) and a multi-core score of 1452.89 (bottom 10%). Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 13.03 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 11.11 GB/sec. Geekbench 6 testing yielded a single-core score of 906.0 and a multi-core score of 1073.0, reflecting limited processing capacity for complex tasks like software compilation (1327.0) and image processing (943.0). For lightweight language model tasks, it processes 164.01 tokens per second for prompts and generates 64.17 tokens per second using a small 135M model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but have minimal memory requirements. The 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it unsuitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. However, it is positioned for lightweight utility workloads, basic static web serving (benchmarked at 1.39 GB/sec), simple Redis key-value operations (1.34 million operations/sec), and small-scale background tasks or microservices that do not demand high memory capacity or local storage.
